standard.title: First Nations music and Country/Place
standard.description: explore how First Nations Australians use music to communicate their connection to and responsibility for Country/Place
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored diverse styles and instruments in First Nations Australian music and examined how music communicates messages about Country/Place (AC9AMU2E02). They can identify instruments and ask basic analytical questions. They have not yet focused on connection to and responsibility for Country/Place as the specific communicative purpose, or engaged with First Nations Australian community protocols for performance.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore how First Nations Australians use music to communicate their connection to and responsibility for Country/Place, including listening expectations and protocols for different contexts.

nodes.label: Music communicating connection to Country/Place
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and describe specific ways that First Nations Australian music communicates connection to Country/Place — including through lyrics, melody, rhythm and instrumentation.
nodes.minimum_width: Listen to one piece of First Nations Australian music connected to Country/Place and identify at least one specific musical element that communicates that connection.
nodes.typical_width: Listen to a diverse range of First Nations Australian music communicating connection to Country/Place — songs with lyrics about Country/Place, music accompanying dances that communicate knowledge; discuss how specific elements (melody, rhythm, texture, instrumentation) serve the communicative purpose; compare different composers' and performers' approaches.
wider: Listen to and explore music that shares feelings about the importance of Country/Place and Story as a starting point for discussing how the same place might be seen and storied differently

Compare two First Nations Australian pieces from different regions or traditions that both connect to Country/Place — what is similar? What is different? What does this reveal about the diversity of connections to Country/Place?
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding that First Nations Australian music communicates specific relationships — connection and responsibility — rather than just emotion or aesthetic effect requires conceptual reframing of what music does. Students who engage with this music only as sonic experience miss the cultural knowledge it carries. This conceptual understanding underpins AC9AMU6E02's investigation of cultural continuity and revitalisation.

response_modes.reason: The concept of 'responsibility for Country/Place' is culturally specific and may be unfamiliar to non-Indigenous students. Use guided questioning — 'What is the music telling us about this place?', 'What does responsibility for Country/Place mean?' — and, where possible, First Nations Australian voices (resources, interviews) to build genuine conceptual understanding rather than a surface-level encounter.

success_criteria: Can describe at least one specific way a musical element communicates connection to Country/Place in a First Nations Australian piece
Can explain the concept of 'connection to Country/Place' in their own words

nodes.label: Learning from First Nations Australians
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can engage with resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians (interviews, podcasts, performances) to learn directly about music and its connection to Country/Place.
nodes.minimum_width: Engage with at least one resource created or co-created by a First Nations Australian person about their music; identify one thing learned directly from that source.
nodes.typical_width: Learn from First Nations Australians about how they use music to communicate connection to Country/Place, culture and people — using interviews, podcasts, performances and co-created resources; distinguish between what they have learned from First Nations sources and what they have inferred or assumed.
wider: Compare learning from a First Nations Australian artist's interview or podcast with listening to their music alone — what additional understanding does hearing directly from them add?
Research a First Nations Australian musician and prepare to share one key thing learned about how their music connects to Country/Place, using the artist's own words where possible

response_modes.reason: The source of knowledge matters in this descriptor. Students who only encounter First Nations Australian music through textbooks or teacher description do not develop the practice of seeking out First Nations Australian voices directly. Each encounter with a co-created or primary source resource builds this practice.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Engaging directly with First Nations Australian voices about their music is a culturally significant practice that goes beyond musical knowledge — it models respectful engagement with knowledge custodians that is relevant across curriculum areas.
success_criteria: Can identify at least one resource created or co-created by First Nations Australians used in learning
Can report at least one specific thing learned from that source (attributed to the source)

nodes.label: Performance protocols and audience responsibilities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the expectations and responsibilities of performers and audiences when experiencing First Nations Australian music that communicates connection to Country/Place.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one protocol or expectation relevant to a specific context of First Nations Australian music performance (e.g. a Welcome to Country).
nodes.typical_width: Learn about expectations and requirements for both performers and audiences in contexts where First Nations Australian music communicates connection to Country/Place — music for Welcome to Country, ceremonial music, community events; discuss why these expectations exist and what they protect.
wider: Compare the expectations for a Welcome to Country with those for a school concert — discuss why the responsibilities are different and why those differences are important
Investigate what it means to engage respectfully as an audience with culturally significant music — identify two or three specific behaviours and explain why each matters

response_modes.reason: Protocol knowledge integrates the conceptual understanding of connection to Country/Place with practical, respectful engagement. Students who understand why protocols exist are more likely to follow them authentically than those who follow rules without understanding their cultural basis.

success_criteria: Can describe at least one protocol or expectation relevant to a First Nations Australian performance context
Can explain why that protocol exists in relation to the music's cultural significance
